lines.line: Taxes on Income, Profit and Capital Gains
Taxes on International Trade and Transactions

revenueMix.source: Saudi Ministry of Finance, Quarterly Budget Performance Report Q4 FY2024, sheet 'Revenues', 'Actual revenues Until Q4 of FY 2024' (SAR million); the same totals in the Year-End Budget Performance Report FY2024 (June 2025, p.13-14)
revenueMix.quote: Oil Revenues 756623.9; Taxes on Income, Profit and Capital Gains 31575.6; Taxes on Goods and Services 288809.2; Taxes on International Trade and Transactions 24498.6; Other Taxes 35645.9; Other Revenues 121942.2; Non-oil Revenues 502471.5; Total 1259095.4. Year-End report p.14: 'In FY2024, the actual total revenue amounted to approximately SAR 1,259 bn ... as oil revenues were recorded at about SAR 757 bn.'
revenueMix.note: The general state budget (the MoF publishes no general-government breakdown). Oil revenue is one line: Aramco's payments of royalties, taxes and dividends (AGSI, 2 July 2025, https://agsi.org/analysis/aramco-and-the-saudi-government-budget/); oil was 62.2% of revenue in 2023. Taxes on goods and services include VAT (about SAR 186 bn), excises (about SAR 16 bn) and the levy on expatriates and dependants (about SAR 40 bn); 'Other Taxes' are mostly corporate zakat; 'Other Revenues' are returns from other government units including the central bank, sales, fees and fines. No personal income tax, social contribution or property tax line exists.
